name: NextDash
description: NextDash is a lightweight, self-hosted bookmark dashboard that features a minimalist, keyboard-driven interface with extensive customization options, making it the perfect personal dashboard for power users. Based on the excellent ThinkDashboard. Key features: • Keyboard-driven navigation for fast access to all your bookmarks • Extensive theme and layout customization, with a look studio beside the dashboard and a theme editor • Inbox to collect new links fast: triage them, or keep them under Bookmarks → Unsorted and file whole groups later • Bookmarks view with Health built in: finds broken, stale and duplicate links, with uptime monitoring and downtime alerts • Video bookmarks marked in the list, and played in the hover card without leaving the dashboard • Widgets beside your bookmarks: 48 built-in kinds (uptime, feeds, weather, calendar, disks, containers and more) plus a Custom widget for any JSON API • Your media stack on the dashboard: Jellyfin, Sonarr, Radarr, Seerr, qBittorrent and SABnzbd, with the posters from your own library • Finds the web apps in your Docker containers and offers them as bookmarks, with an icon and a status check (needs the Docker socket below) • Glances on the dashboard: a page for the hosts you run Glances on, with processes, containers, graphs and incidents, and a widget for one host • Your Unraid server on the dashboard: seven widgets for the array, parity, shares, VMs, the UPS and notifications, with alerts • Web search in the search panel through your own SearXNG or the Brave Search API • Six interface languages: English, Dutch, German, French, Spanish and Chinese • Lightweight and fast, no heavy dependencies • Actively maintained with regular releases Links: • Website: https://www.nextdash.cc • Source code and releases: https://github.com/jordibrouwer/nextdash • Changelog: https://github.com/jordibrouwer/nextdash/releases • Devlog / release updates: https://www.nextdash.cc/news • Also available on GHCR: ghcr.io/jordibrouwer/nextdash:latest • User manual: https://github.com/jordibrouwer/nextdash/blob/main/MANUAL.md The host widgets (Processor, Memory, Disks, Containers) are off until you fill in the optional paths and variables below — they are hidden under Show more settings. Section 15.4 of the manual explains what each one reads. Support: open an issue on GitHub via the Support link above. Bug reports and feature requests are welcome.

paths.name: AppData
paths.description: Persistent storage path for NextDash data (bookmarks, settings)

paths.name: Host proc
paths.description: Optional. Mount the host /proc here for the Processor and Memory widgets. Host path: /proc

paths.name: Host disks
paths.description: Optional. Mount the array here for the Disks widget. Host path: /mnt — then name /mnt/user or /mnt/cache in the widget.

paths.name: Docker socket
paths.description: Optional. Mount the Docker socket here for the Containers widget. Host path: /var/run/docker.sock — read-only still exposes the daemon's whole read API, so use a socket proxy if that is too much.

ports.name: WebUI Port
ports.description: Port for the NextDash web interface

variables.name: Write token
variables.description: Optional. Require this token in the X-NextDash-Token header on every write. Leave empty for an open instance on a trusted network.

variables.name: Trusted proxies
variables.description: Optional. Addresses and CIDR ranges whose X-Forwarded-For header is believed, comma-separated — set this if nextDash sits behind a reverse proxy, so rate limits count per visitor instead of per proxy. Left empty the header is ignored.

variables.name: Allowed hosts
variables.description: Optional. Only with a write token: public host names the dashboard may be opened by, comma-separated (*.example.com allowed, * turns the check off). IP addresses, localhost and private names (.local, .lan) always work. Needed when you open nextDash by your own domain.

variables.name: Host proc variable
variables.description: Optional. Set to /host/proc once the mount above is filled in.

variables.name: Host root variable
variables.description: Optional. Set to /host/root once the disks mount above is filled in.

variables.name: Docker socket variable
variables.description: Optional. Set to /var/run/docker.sock once the socket mount above is filled in. Unset, the Containers widget is hidden.

variables.name: Docker actions
variables.description: Optional. 1 lets the Containers view start, stop, update and remove containers; 0 keeps it read-only. A writable socket is root on the host, so set a write token as well.

variables.name: Run as root
variables.description: Optional. 1 keeps nextDash running as root, needed only when the Docker socket belongs to root's group (gid 0). Unraid's socket belongs to the docker group (gid 281), so leave this at 0 here.
